bib.title: Generative Multimodal Models are In-Context Learners

question: Can scaling a generative multimodal model trained with one autoregressive objective over text tokens and continuous visual embeddings give strong task-agnostic in-context learning across understanding and generation?
hypothesis: A scaled-up generative pretrained multimodal model can harness in-context learning abilities like those of large language models and generalize to unseen multimodal tasks.
contributions: Emu2, a 37B generative multimodal model trained with a predict-the-next-multimodal-element objective
State-of-the-art few-shot results on several VQA datasets; Emu2-Chat (instruction-tuned) and Emu2-Gen (controllable generation) derived from it
Simpler architecture than Emu: mean pooling plus linear projection replaces C-Former

method.summary: Emu2 joins an EVA-02-CLIP-E-plus visual encoder, a LLaMA-33B decoder and an SDXL-base visual decoder. Images become 64 continuous embeddings interleaved with text tokens; text is trained with classification loss and image embeddings with regression loss. The decoder is trained separately as an autoencoder detokenizer, then Emu2 is instruction tuned into Emu2-Chat and Emu2-Gen.
method.task: unified autoregressive multimodal pretraining (text tokens and visual embeddings), VQA, chat, grounded and subject-driven image generation

datasets.name: MMC4, YT-Storyboard-1B (interleaved)
datasets.preprocessing: per MMC4 document N=8 images sampled to build a subsequence of L=1024; image placed before or after its text with p=0.5

datasets.name: GRIT-20M, CapsFusion-grounded-100M
datasets.preprocessing: coordinates as 224 discrete tokens; phrase placed before or after coordinates with p=0.7

datasets.name: LAION-COCO, LAION-Aesthetics
datasets.preprocessing: drop images below 512x512; ratio-preserving random scale then square random crop; original size and crop coordinates as extra conditions (SDXL)

datasets.name: Chat data: COCO Caption, TextCaps, VQAv2, OKVQA, GQA, TextVQA, M3IT, RefCOCO/+/g, LLaVA, LLaVAR, ShareGPT, Alpaca, VideoChat, clock reading

Generation data: CapsFusion-grounded-100M, GRIT (SAM-segmented subset ~5M), InstructPix2Pix, CapsFusion, LAION-Aesthetics, SA-1B, LAION-High-Resolution; ~500k premium pairs (Unsplash, Midjourney-V5, DALL-E-3)
MS-COCO val, DreamBench, VQAv2, OKVQA, VizWiz, TextVQA, HatefulMemes, GQA, MSVD, MSRVTT, SEED-Bench, MM-Vet, TouchStone, MMMU, RefCOCO family
datasets.size: 30k COCO val prompts; DreamBench 4 images x prompts = 3,000

models.name: Emu2
models.architecture: EVA-02-CLIP-E-plus encoder + LLaMA-33B decoder + SDXL-base visual decoder; mean pool each image to 8x8 (pretraining) or 16x16 (instruction tuning) tokens then linear projection
models.tokenizer: LLaMA tokenizer plus added special and <loc> tokens

models.name: Emu2-Gen
models.architecture: Emu2 tuned with regression loss on last image embeddings; decoder is SDXL-based

models.name: Flamingo 9B/80B, IDEFICS 80B, Kosmos-1/2, Emu 14B, Qwen-VL, LLaVA-1.5, CogVLM, SDXL, SDv1.5, DALL-E 3, GILL, SEED, Kosmos-G, BLIP-Diffusion

training.objective: Stage 1: captioning loss on text tokens only. Stage 2 and tuning: text classification (cross-entropy) loss plus image regression loss on visual embeddings; Chat supervises only the <Answer> tokens; Gen applies regression loss only to the last image. Visual decoder: image autoencoding (diffusion loss) conditioned on the 64 embeddings.
training.optimizer: AdamW; pretrain beta1=0.9 beta2=0.95 eps=1e-6; Chat beta2=0.98; decoder beta2=0.999 eps 1e-8, weight decay 0.01
training.lr: Stage 1 peak 1e-4 (linear projection), 3e-5 (LLaMA), 5e-5 (visual encoder); stage 2 1e-5; Chat 1e-5; Gen 5e-5 then 1e-5 (quality fine-tuning); decoder 1e-4
training.lr_schedule: cosine decay (pretrain, Chat, Gen); log warm-up then linear decay (decoder)
training.warmup: ratio 0.02 (stage 1), 0.1 (stage 2); Chat 100 steps; Gen 100 steps in text (Table 9 ratio 0.0); decoder 2,000 in text vs 2,500 in Table 7
training.batch_size: Stage 1: 6,144 image-text, 768 video-text; stage 2: 12,800 / 6,400 / 3,200 interleaved / 800 language; Chat 768; Gen 4,096 (500k QFT 2,048); decoder 2,048
training.steps: Stage 1 35,200 at 224px plus 4,000 at 448px; stage 2 20,350; Chat 8k; Gen 3k plus 900 quality fine-tuning; decoder 8,000 (2,000+6,000 in text)
training.tokens: stage 2: about 160 million image-text samples and 3.8B language-only tokens
training.regularisation: gradient clip 5.0 (pretrain, Chat), 1.0 (Gen, decoder); classifier-free guidance by dropping image embeddings with 10% probability; noise offset 0.1; random drop of entity tokens and localization images in Gen

other.stage_structure: Stage 1 trains encoder, projection and LLaMA; stage 2 freezes the visual encoder
other.decoder_training: SDXL VAE and visual encoder frozen, only U-Net updated; encoder input 448x448, output 1024x1024
other.video_decoder: 3D U-Net from Stable Diffusion 2.1 with 1D temporal conv after each 2D conv, fully trained; no hyperparameters given
other.chat_frames: 8, 12 or 16 frames sampled per video in training

inference.decoding: Chat: beam size 5; generation: EulerDiscreteScheduler, 50 diffusion steps
inference.samples: DreamBench: 4 images per prompt, 3,000 total; MM-Vet averaged over five scoring runs
inference.prompting: Few-shot examples chosen by RICES, separated by a period, prompt '[image] based on the picture, [question] short answer:'
inference.retrieval: RICES (Retrieval In-Context Example Selection) for few-shot selection

metrics.name: VQA score / EM / accuracy / ROC AUC / GPT-4 score
CLIP-I
metrics.definition: CLIP-ViT-L image similarity to real image (GILL protocol)

eval.protocol: Single runs, no seeds or significance tests stated; MM-Vet and TouchStone scored by GPT-4.

availability.data: public datasets plus unreleased ~500k quality set

prompts.text: [image] based on the picture, [question] short answer:
[image] based on the picture, answer in one word or phrase. [question] short answer:
You are a helpful assistant, dedicated to provide concise and efficient answers.

limits: In-context learning can fail in complex scenes such as counting in a crowd (Appendix A).
Gap to closed systems conceded: GPT-4V 67.7 vs Emu2 48.5 on MM-Vet.
Hallucination, biased or harmful generation inherited from training data.
Hardware, compute, wall clock, seeds and layer/hidden sizes are not stated; no ablations (e.g. pooling vs C-Former, 8x8 vs 16x16 tokens) are reported.
Zero-shot VQA is weak (VQAv2 33.5) unless the prompt is tuned; Emu2-Chat marks asterisks where task training sets were used, so Table 2 mixes seen and unseen data.
Generation scored only with CLIP-I, CLIP-T and DINO, no human or FID evaluation; text prompt-following trails SDXL and DALL-E 3.
Table 1 base-model comparison uses RICES-selected shots; benchmark contamination checks are not described.
